disease_label_per_paper: Right lower-extremity cellulitis / skin and soft tissue infection with Pseudomonas putida bacteremia
presentation_summary: 63-year-old man with well-controlled diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, stage IV CKD, and a chronic right lower-extremity wound presented with four days of worsening right lower-leg swelling, erythema, and non-purulent discharge.
He had been treated as cellulitis with oral cephalexin for seven days without improvement and reported intermittent fevers.
Physical examination showed edema and erythema from the ankle to mid-thigh with tenderness and no crepitus.
Labs showed WBC 31.4 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 9 g/dL, creatinine 5.54 mg/dL, eGFR 11, and lactate 2.3 mmol/L.
CT with contrast showed circumferential subcutaneous edema from lower thigh to foot but no necrotizing infection or drainable abscess.
